ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Alpine Valley show featuring iconic Music>Sugaree>Music and a soaring Wheel
ai_show_review.blurb: The August ’82 Alpine Valley concert delivers the celebrated Music → Sugaree → Music segue, tight transitions and an explosive second set highlighted by China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider, The Wheel and a Playin’ sandwich. Jerry’s vocals are on fire while Brent’s keyboards add texture throughout. Soundboard sources capture the band in crisp, high‑energy form.
ai_show_review.review:
What unfolds at Alpine Valley on August 7 1982 is a quintessential early‑80s Dead night: the first set rolls out with a rare Music Never Stopped → Sugaree → Music sequence that showcases Jerry’s soaring vocal phrasing and razor‑sharp lead work. The band rides that momentum into a solid run of classics – Me And My Uncle, Big River, Althea and Let It Grow – each delivered with tight interplay and an unmistakable sense of excitement.

The second set kicks into overdrive. China Cat Sunflower seamlessly segues into I Know You Rider before launching into a powerful The Wheel that is driven by Mickey and Billy’s thunderous drumming. A Playin’ In The Band sandwich bookends an expansive Space, culminating in a fiery Morning Dew that feels both urgent and lyrical. Brent’s keyboards weave spacey textures while Phil’s bass, though occasionally muddy on audience tapes, provides the deep groove that anchors the improvisations. Overall the show is a high‑octane snapshot of the band at a creative peak, captured best by the crystal‑clear soundboard recordings.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard source with crisp, clean mix and no dropouts; captures the band’s high energy and tight performance better than other tapes.

key_highlights: Iconic Music → Sugaree → Music segue with Jerry’s soaring vocals and tight band play
The Wheel delivers a thunderous, driving performance powered by Mickey and Billy’s drumming
China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider and the Playin’ sandwich showcase explosive second‑set improvisation
Crystal‑clear soundboard recordings preserve the high‑energy atmosphere with excellent detail

band_performance.Jerry: Vocals are on fire throughout, especially during the Music> Sugaree >Music sequence; lead guitar work is crisp, melodic and drives the high‑energy vibe of both sets.
band_performance.Phil: Bass provides a solid foundation with booming leads on The Wheel, though some recordings note occasional muddiness or moments out of sync in the first set.
band_performance.Bob: Rhythm guitar stays solid and supportive; backing vocals add intensity during second‑set breaks, contributing to the overall tightness.
band_performance.Brent: Keyboards shine in spacey passages and the Playin’ sandwich, adding texture and melodic depth that elevate the improvisations.
band_performance.Mickey: Drumming is repeatedly praised as one of the best of the night—tight, powerful and a driving force behind The Wheel and the second‑set flow.
band_performance.Billy: Provides fierce, propulsive rhythm alongside Mickey; his energy fuels the explosive jams and keeps the band locked in.
